Message Intermediate Throw Event

General Concept: A Message Intermediate Throw Event in BPMN is used to send a message during process execution, without ending the process. It is typically used for notifications, integration, or signaling other processes or systems at intermediate points in the workflow.

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, a Message Intermediate Throw Event sends a message at a specific point in the process. You can define output mappings using FEEL expressions to prepare the message payload. The engine supports error handling and ensures only mapped variables are sent. Message Intermediate Throw Events can interact with messaging systems, APIs, or custom adapters for outbound communication.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
A Message Intermediate Throw Event in TaktX allows you to:

  • Define output mappings using FEEL expressions to prepare the message payload.
  • Configure error handling and delivery options for reliable notification.
  • Limit variable scope to only mapped variables for security and clarity.
  • Integrate with messaging systems, APIs, or custom adapters for outbound communication.
  • Monitor execution and audit results via the TaktX client.
  • Attach boundary events for error, escalation, or timer handling if needed.

Example: Partner Notification with Message Intermediate Throw Event

 

This example shows a process where, after a review, a Message Intermediate Throw Event notifies a partner system before the process continues to completion. This demonstrates mid-process outbound integration.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use FEEL expressions to format and validate message payloads.
  • Configure error handling for reliable delivery.
  • Document message formats and endpoints.

Pitfalls:

  • Unmapped variables will not be included in the message.
  • Handle delivery errors to avoid missing notifications.
  • Ensure message endpoints are reachable and properly secured.
